slides.title: Q4 Customer Churn Overview
slides.speaker_note: Focus on the strategic imperative: churn is accelerating and requires immediate executive attention.

slides.title: Executive Summary

bullets: Customer churn increased to 5.2% in Q4, up from 4.6% in Q3
Continuous upward trend observed throughout the year (Q1: 4.1% → Q4: 5.2%)
Residential customer segment shows highest churn acceleration
Three primary drivers identified: price sensitivity, communication gaps, and competitive pressure
Immediate strategic intervention required to reverse trend

slides.speaker_note: Emphasize that this is not a one-quarter blip—it's a sustained trend that demands action.

slides.title: Quarterly Churn Progression
slides.speaker_note: Point out the consistent quarter-over-quarter increase. The slope is steepening, not flattening.

slides.title: Primary Churn Drivers

bullets: Price sensitivity remains the dominant factor driving customer exits
Communication issues indicate gaps in customer engagement and support responsiveness
Competitive offers suggest our value proposition requires reinforcement
Residential segment particularly vulnerable to all three drivers
Combined effect creates compound risk in customer base stability

slides.speaker_note: These are not isolated issues—they reinforce each other. A customer frustrated by communication is more price-sensitive.

slides.title: Observations & Implications

left_column.heading: What We Observe
items: Churn rate increased 0.6 percentage points in one quarter

right_column.heading: What It Means
items: Revenue risk compounding if trend continues
Customer acquisition costs not offset by retention
Market positioning weakening in core segment

slides.speaker_note: Translate the numbers into business impact. This is about revenue, profitability, and competitive position.

slides.title: Strategic Retention Plan

content.recommendation: Implement targeted retention program focused on residential segment with pricing flexibility and proactive communication
rationale: Residential segment represents highest churn acceleration and immediate intervention opportunity
Price sensitivity can be addressed through tiered offers and loyalty incentives
Communication improvements deliver quick wins with minimal capital investment
next_steps: Launch customer feedback program within 2 weeks to validate drivers
Develop competitive pricing analysis and retention offer framework
Implement proactive outreach protocol for at-risk residential accounts

slides.speaker_note: This recommendation balances quick wins (communication) with strategic positioning (pricing). Emphasize the 2-week timeline for feedback.

slides.title: Data Sources & Methodology

items: Churn reasons: Exit survey responses and support ticket analysis
Residential segment: Defined as non-business accounts

slides.speaker_note: All data has been validated and cross-referenced. Exit surveys had 68% response rate.
